The 144 and 151W sizes appear in multiple US retailer listings. [20][MERCHANT] 29. Shape: True Twin [21] 30. Shape description: Completely symmetrical shape — "a true-twin shape and camber profile help this snowboard feel the same going regular as it does switch" [21] 31. Camber type (2024): Twin Combination Camber — camber between the feet with rockered tip and tail [22] 32. Camber description: "By blending both traditional Camber and Rocker profiles, Combination Camber gives you all the benefits of both: the pop and precision of camber, and the float and predictability of rocker" [23] 33. Profile description (K2 manufacturer): "Outfitted with camber between the feet the Geometric gives riders pop and energy, while a rockered tip-and-tail makes it catch-free and easy to press" [21] 34. DISAGREEMENT — Camber type (2025): One retailer (Ski Barn Durango) describes the 2025 model as having a "Flat-to-Rocker Profile" rather than Combination Camber. Most other sources continue to describe it as Rocker/Camber/Rocker (Combination Camber). This may indicate a spec change for 2025, or a retailer error. [24] 35. Profile symmetry: Symmetrical camber profile throughout the length of the board [25] 36. Setback all sizes: 0mm (centered stance, consistent with true twin) [MERCHANT] 37. Taper: 0mm implied (true twin — nose and tail widths identical per size) [MERCHANT] 38. Flex rating (2024 merchant data): 6/10 [MERCHANT] 39. DISAGREEMENT — Flex rating (2025 model per Backcountry/Steep&Cheap): "soft (3 out of 10 on K2's scale)" [26]. This is a major disagreement with the merchant data which states 6/10 for the 2024 model. This may be a genuine spec change between model years or data inconsistency. BaseNZ also describes a "forgiving 3/10 flex rating" for the 2025 model [27]. 40. Evo flex classification: "Medium" (evo classifies manufacturer ratings of 3-5 as medium, 6-8 as stiff) [28] 41. Flex description (K2): "softer flexing twin predictable and pressable" [21] 42. Flex pattern: Consistent throughout — "A single species of wood ensures a consistent flex pattern" [29] 43. Flex direction: Twin (symmetrical flex) [21] 44. Core material: Aspen wood — single species [30] 45. Core description: "A single species lightweight wood core that delivers smooth flex and lively rebound" [31] 46. Core construction: Single-species wood core (no multi-wood blend) [30] 47. Fiberglass type: Biax Glass (Biaxial Fiberglass) [32] 48. Fiberglass configuration: Fibres woven at 0° and 90° [33] 49. Fiberglass description: "A lightweight glass layup at 0° and 90° for a consistent, smooth flex" — "Smooth all-purpose performance with a no-frills design" [33][34] 50. Sidewall construction: Hybritech Sidewall Construction — K2 exclusive [35] 51. Sidewall technology description: "By transitioning from a P-Tex sidewall into a capped construction in the tip and tail of our snowboards, we can reduce waste while giving our snowboards better energy transfer and making them more durable" [35] 52. Hybritech detail: "Removing all excess sidewall material in the tip and tail and adding a 3D capped edge to increase the bond strength of the fiberglass and decrease the swing weight of the board" [36] 53. Base material: Extruded 2000 Base [37] 54. Base description: "A low maintenance and smooth gliding base material that's durable and easy to repair" [31] 55. Base maintenance: Low-maintenance, easy to repair — "easy to repair for those early season core shots when you're jibbing whatever is available" [21] 56. Insert configuration: 2x4 mounting pattern [MERCHANT][38] 57. Insert description: "2x4 Insert packs allow for secure binding mounting while optimizing stance-width options" [38] 58. Edge hold: Camber underfoot increases contact length with snow to improve edge hold [25] 102. Catch-free ride: Rockered tip and tail makes it "catch-free and easy to press" [21] 103. Switch riding: True twin shape ensures same feel regular and switch [21] 104. Responsiveness: Described as "predictable and pressable" rather than highly responsive [21] 105. Stability: Twin-tip shape "feels stable and balanced whether riding regular or switch" [39] 106. Target use case: "the perfect tool for those looking for an affordable twin-tip, softer-flexing freestyle board or someone that has caught the snowboard bug and is looking to drop in on their first complete set-up" [21] 107. Whitelines review (2021-22 model): "The Geometric board is the perfect tool if you want a high-performance freestyle board that sits at an affordable price point" [40] 108. Whitelines review positive: "This board would make a great first snowboard, suitable for beginners but it will take a long time to outgrow" [40] 109. Whitelines review — forgiving flex: "With a more forgiving flex it's ideal for learning new tricks and progressing your skills in and out of the park" [40] 110. Whitelines construction review: "It's simple yet highly effective, providing everything you need in a freestyle board" [41] 111. Backcountry/Steep&Cheap review: "The Geometric is one of the best starter freestyle boards I've tested. It's super easy to press and poppy without being unstable" [42] 112. Looria aggregate rating: C grade based on 2 reviews [43] 113. Looria sentiment summary: "Great for flat ground tricks. Soft and playful. Good value for the money." [43] 114. K2 official review (YouTube): "it's an amazing board for that entry, beginner, intermediate level rider, someone who's in the park who wants that super so[ft flex]" [43] 115. Backcountry editorial: "Affordable, reliable, and fun to ride—this board keeps us coming back for more" [44] 116. evo description: "a softer-flexing board aimed squarely at aspiring park riders on their way up" [23] 117. Level Nine Sports Gearhead review: "Its true twin flex and camber profile really stood out, making it a go-to for playful maneuvers in the park. It's perfect for riders who love a mix of stability and fun." [18] 118. K2 ski/snowboard warranty: 2 years from original date of purchase for defects in materials and workmanship [45] 119. K2 warranty coverage: Structural cracks to top sheet, base, core, edge, and sidewall due to manufacturing defect; delaminating due to manufacturing defect [45] 120. K2 warranty exclusions: "Any problem resulting from impact, misuse, abuse, or neglect. This includes but is not limited to boxes, rails, and rock damage" — this is notable for a park/jib board [45] 121. Warranty note: evo listed K2 Geometric 2023 as having a "3 Years" warranty, which may differ from the general K2 policy [46] 122. DISAGREEMENT — Warranty period: K2's official warranty page states 2 years for skis and snowboards, but evo lists 3 years for K2 products. A Newschoolers forum user also claims "K2 has a 2 or 3 year warranty." The exact warranty for snowboards specifically may differ from the general K2 policy page. [45][46][47] 123. Warranty original purchaser only: "K2 Snowboarding warranties are reserved for the original purchaser only" [48] 124. K2 brand heritage: "K2 is the original American Ski and Snowboard Brand, founded in 1962 in Washington State" [6] 125. K2 snowboard start: K2 expanded into snowboards in 1987 [6] 126. K2 women's innovation: "The first brand to specifically engineer products for women starting in 1999" [6] 127. K2 parent company sister brands: Elevate Outdoor Collective includes K2 Skis, K2 Snowboards, Marker, Dalbello, Völkl, RIDE Snowboards, LINE Skis, and others [4] 128. K2 ownership history: Founded on Vashon Island → Jarden Corporation (2007) → Newell Brands → Kohlberg & Company (2017) → Now operates as Elevate Outdoor Collective [5][49] 129. K2 sustainability commitment: "K2 is dedicated to reducing our environmental footprint... strive to use eco-friendly materials, minimise waste" [50] 130. K2 lineup positioning: The Geometric sits in K2's beginner/freestyle category alongside the Standard, First Lite, World Peace, and Lime Lite [51] 131. Within-brand alternative (all-mountain beginner): K2 Gateway — "an easy riding board that offers easy turn initiation and a really versatile shape" for those wanting all-mountain versatility instead of freestyle focus [52] 132. Within-brand alternative (freestyle step-up): K2 Afterblack — for more advanced freestyle riders wanting more durability [53] 133. Comparable competitor: YES Basic — "a great little freestyle board that is also well suited to beginners. It has a nice forgiving medium-soft flex" [54] 134. Comparable competitor: Rome Mechanic — another freestyle-oriented beginner option that "feels a bit more planted underfoot" [55] 135. Comparable competitor: Burton Instigator / Cultivator — Burton's beginner-focused offerings; "The Cultivator embodies everything it means to be a good beginner board" [56] 136. Comparable competitor: Nitro Prime — a budget-friendly beginner option [56] 137. Comparable competitor: Ride Agenda — "very much a freestyle snowboard" with "easy going hybrid camber profile" and soft 3/10 flex [52] 138. evo: Established major US online retailer, reputable for snowboard sales, offers expert advice and size charts [23] 139. Backcountry/Steep&Cheap: Major US outdoor retailer with detailed specs, editorial reviews [42] 140. Level Nine Sports: Reputable US retailer offering lowest price guarantee and free shipping over $50 [15] 141. The House: Established US retailer with long history in action sports [16] 142. Milosport: Specialty snowboard shop in Salt Lake City with strong local reputation, offers in-store pickup [14] 143. Amazon: Major marketplace retailer; board listed from K2 directly [6] 144. BaseNZ: New Zealand specialty retailer [39] 145. Snowtrax: UK specialty snowboard store [50] 146. Value positioning: Positioned as an affordable entry-level freestyle board, lower price point within K2 lineup [21] 147. Construction simplicity: Uses basic (non-premium) construction — no carbon, sintered base, or advanced core — keeping cost down [41] 148. Base type limitation: Extruded base (rather than sintered) — slower base speed but more durable and easier to repair; typical for entry-level boards [37] 149. Progression potential: "suitable for beginners but it will take a long time to outgrow" [40] 150. Design philosophy: Clean, geometric-inspired aesthetic consistent with model name [9] 151. Topsheet material: Standard topsheet with Hybritech capped construction in tip and tail [35]
